log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon
|-damage|p2a: Incineroar|87/100|[from] ability: Rough Skin|[of] p1a: Garchomp

decisions.thought: This is team preview, so I need three Pokémon. Incineroar leads for Intimidate and Fake Out to blunt the opponent's physical attackers. Garchomp is the fastest threat and can Mega, and Gholdengo adds a strong special attacker to cover the Steel/Dark and Grass types.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: I need to pick three mons against an opponent likely mirroring a similar team. Incineroar offers intimidate and utility, Garchomp brings speed and setup, and Kingambit hits hard as a late-game threat — that trio seems like a solid core against their Garchomp/Kingambit/Archaludon/Gholdengo lineup.

decisions.thought: Opposing Garchomp outspeeds Incineroar (109-169 vs 80), so it could hit first. Fake Out has +3 priority and is legal on Incineroar's first turn, so it flinches Garchomp before it acts. Incineroar's Intimidate has already cut its Attack.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Fake Out on Garchomp seems like a solid opening move since it's legal turn one and will flinch Garchomp, locking it out of acting while also chipping some damage, factoring in possible Rough Skin recoil from the contact.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp is faster than Incineroar, and Earthquake hits Incineroar for 2x. Flare Blitz only does half damage to this Dragon/Ground target. Protect blocks this turn's attack, scouts their move, and keeps Incineroar's Attack drop.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking Garchomp's matchup against Incineroar - it's slower with Atk lowered by Intimidate, and I need to verify whether Earthquake hits Incineroar hard given its Fire/Dark typing isn't actually weak to Ground.

Then I'm weighing whether Gholdengo could switch in safely instead, since its Steel/Ghost typing is quadruple weak to Ground from Earthquake, which rules that out, leaving Shadow Ball as a weak neutral option against Garchomp.

Now I'm checking if Incineroar's Flare Blitz is resisted by Garchomp's Dragon/Ground typing.

Weighing Protect to stall a turn versus Parting Shot to pivot, considering our own Garchomp would still take double damage from an opposing Dragon-type move. Leaning toward Parting Shot into Gholdengo despite the Ground weakness since it still lowers the opposing Garchomp's offense further.

Weighing the risk either way, I'll just go with Protect for safety this turn to scout their move before committing.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp outspeeds Incineroar, and Flare Blitz is resisted by its Dragon typing. Parting Shot lowers its Attack again, and Gholdengo can take the hit and act afterward.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Mega Garchomp's Earthquake is a real threat to Incineroar even with its attack lowered by Intimidate, so I'm weighing whether to Protect again or risk attacking this turn.

Considering Parting Shot to switch out and let Gholdengo absorb the hit, though its Steel typing makes it 2x weak to Ground. Also weighing Flare Blitz, which is resisted by Garchomp's Dragon typing but not its Ground part, against an already-damaged Garchomp.

Gholdengo's bulk (115 Def, 164 HP) should let it survive even a reduced Earthquake, so Parting Shot into Gholdengo seems like the safer play over Protect.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp outspeeds Incineroar and Earthquake would finish it, so Incineroar must switch. Our Garchomp is a poor answer because Ground and Dragon are both super effective against Dragon/Ground. Gholdengo at 164 HP with Life Orb and Special Attack 203 can take an Earthquake at -2 Attack and threaten a strong Make It Rain or Shadow Ball next turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Incineroar is low and weak to Ground, and Mega Garchomp will likely hit again with Earthquake, so I should consider switching. Gholdengo as Steel/Ghost takes Ground damage neutrally, making it a safer option than staying in.

Actually Garchomp matching up against itself is bad since Dragon/Ground takes 2x from both Dragon and Ground moves. Gholdengo seems like the safer call — it can tank the Earthquake at reduced attack and threaten back without taking Dragon damage, so with Incineroar already fulfilling its role via Parting Shot, I'll bring in Gholdengo.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo is faster than Garchomp in most spreads, and Make It Rain (120 BP, STAB, Life Orb) should deal roughly 160 damage, close to the opponent's remaining HP. Shadow Ball would fall short, and Thunderbolt does nothing to a Ground type. The self-drop from Make It Rain is acceptable if it secures the knockout.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Garchomp's at 87% with attack and special attack dropped. Since Gholdengo is Steel-type, it's weak to Ground moves like Earthquake, but it's immune to status thanks to Good as Gold. I'll go with Thunderbolt here.

Actually, Electric does nothing to Ground-type Garchomp. Shadow Ball would be neutral but doesn't hit hard enough to KO given Garchomp's SpD—I'm estimating around 111-164 damage with Life Orb depending on the move, not quite enough against its remaining HP of roughly 174. Make It Rain could nearly KO while also dropping its Special Attack further, which seems like the stronger option, though Garchomp's own Earthquake would still hit Gholdengo hard in return.

Also checking Incineroar's HP at 82 and considering Garchomp's Earthquake there instead. I'll go with Make It Rain as the choice, confirming Sand Force doesn't matter since there's no sandstorm up.

decisions.thought: Mega Incineroar is Fire/Dark, so Make It Rain and Shadow Ball are weak here. Gholdengo at 28 HP will likely die to the next hit, and Thunderbolt won't secure a KO. Garchomp switches in healthy, outspeeds Incineroar, and Earthquake is 2x super effective on Fire.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
The opponent's Incineroar is Mega Evolved, now Fire/Dark with Darkest Lariat. My Gholdengo is at 28 HP, and I'm weighing Make It Rain's effectiveness—Steel is resisted by Fire but neutral against Dark, so I need to check if Steel resists coming back at it too.

Thunderbolt looks like my best move since it's neutral against both Fire and Dark, and Gholdengo should outspeed Mega Incineroar given its low base speed. Still, any hit likely KOs Gholdengo at 28 HP, so I'm considering switching to Garchomp at full health instead, since Earthquake would hit the Fire typing for super effective damage and Garchomp outspeeds Incineroar easily.

Garchomp switching in would land Earthquake for solid super-effective damage on Mega Incineroar, likely 60-70% of its HP. Since Gholdengo at 28 HP will die to basically anything anyway, switching to preserve it as a future threat with Thunderbolt seems like the better play than trading it now.

decisions.thought: Garchomp is faster (169 vs at most 123), so it moves first. Earthquake is super effective on Fire/Dark Incineroar and should knock out what remains of it at 77% HP. Mega Evolving adds attack and makes the Garchomp evolution permanent, so Mega Earthquake is the strongest choice.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm recalling that the opponent's Incineroar is Mega Evolved, retaining Fire/Dark typing and Intimidate, with boosted HP and Attack stats to factor into this matchup.

Garchomp, sitting at 123/185 HP with Rough Skin, is Dragon/Ground, so Earthquake gets STAB and is also super effective against Incineroar's Fire typing. I'm working through the damage calculation for a Mega Garchomp Earthquake against Incineroar's defense to see if it threatens a KO at 77% HP (~155 of 202).

Even across Incineroar's possible defense range, the calc shows Earthquake lands close to or above 155 damage, suggesting a likely KO either way. Mega Evolving boosts Garchomp's attack further for extra security, though it costs a turn — not a concern here since Garchomp outspeeds. I'm leaning toward using Mega Earthquake to guarantee the knockout given Incineroar is the only active threat left.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp (158 Speed) outspeeds Incineroar, which is at about 156 HP. Earthquake is super effective and 100% accurate, so it should knock out Incineroar before it can act. Stone Edge has only 80% accuracy.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Mega Garchomp at 158 speed outspeeds the opponent's Incineroar, which sits around 156 HP. Earthquake should be super effective against Incineroar's Fire typing, so I'm calculating the damage using Garchomp's 222 attack with STAB and the 2x type bonus against Incineroar's defense in the 110-156 range.

Working through the damage formula at level 50 with the STAB and super-effective multipliers, I get roughly 230 damage, which should comfortably knock out Incineroar's 156 HP. Earthquake has perfect accuracy versus Stone Edge's 80%, so even though Incineroar might protect again, Earthquake is the clear choice this turn.

decisions.thought: Mega Garchomp outspeeds Archaludon (158 vs 94-150 possible), so it moves first. Earthquake is super effective against Steel and neutral against Dragon, making it the strongest hit. Stone Edge and Outrage are weaker here.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Mega Garchomp outspeeds Archaludon and hits hard with Earthquake, which is super effective against its Steel typing despite the Sturdy risk at full HP. Stone Edge is weaker here, so Earthquake remains the better option; Outrage is also viable against the Dragon/Steel typing but less optimal than EQ.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is at 5% and its Draco Meteor is weakened by the -2 SpA drop. Incineroar has 82 HP, so it should survive one hit, then Flare Blitz (2x vs Steel) knocks it out. Gholdengo's 28 HP would die to any hit.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing whether to switch to Gholdengo at low HP or keep Incineroar in against the mega Archaludon, checking speed tiers since Archaludon's mega form could outspeed my options depending on its stat spread.

Electric coverage from Gholdengo would hit Archaludon super effectively (Steel/Dragon takes 2x from Thunderbolt), so if Gholdengo is faster that's a clean KO on an opponent already at 5% HP, but I'm not fully certain of the speed comparison given Archaludon's possible range.

Considering Incineroar as the switch-in instead: Draco Meteor at -2 SpA would still deal considerable damage to its 82 HP given Archaludon's high base SpA, though it's unclear if Incineroar survives, and afterward Incineroar's Flare Blitz would be super effective against Steel-type Archaludon and likely finish it off given its sliver of HP remaining. Fake Out wouldn't help here since it's Normal-type and doesn't threaten a KO.

I'll go with switching to Incineroar.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is slower than the Mega Archaludon, which is at 5% HP. Fake Out has +3 priority and this is Incineroar's first turn on the field, so it moves first. Even a modest hit from the 40 BP move should finish off a Pokémon with only about 9 HP left.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Archaludon's Mega form with Stamina outspeeds Incineroar, but Flare Blitz being Fire against Steel/Dragon works out to neutral damage overall, and with 183 Attack it would likely deal massive damage at 5% HP regardless.

But wait — Incineroar just switched in, so Fake Out is available: priority +3, 40 BP Normal-type, neutral damage against Steel, and the flinch prevents Archaludon from attacking. Since Archaludon is already at 5% HP, Fake Out's damage alone should finish it off before it can act, making that the clear choice.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is at 1% but is faster than Incineroar, and its Draco Meteor would likely KO our 82 HP Incineroar before Flare Blitz lands. Protect (+4 priority) blocks this turn's attack, and any later damage will finish the 1% Archaludon.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Archaludon is at 1% HP and faster, so it can Draco Meteor for the KO before Incineroar's Flare Blitz lands. Protect would stall a turn, but with Archaludon this low, any chip damage next turn finishes it off regardless.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is at 1% and outspeeds Incineroar, so Flare Blitz would likely be preempted by a Draco Meteor that could KO my 82 HP Incineroar. Protect blocks that attack this turn and keeps Incineroar alive to finish the 1% Archaludon next turn.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Archaludon is at 1% HP but Incineroar is slower, so whatever Archaludon does will resolve first. Flare Blitz should KO regardless of Stamina's defense boost, but Archaludon might protect again, or fire off Draco Meteor which likely one-shots Incineroar given its SpA versus Incineroar's SpD.

I'm also weighing switching to Gholdengo via Parting Shot — it could threaten a kill with Shadow Ball or Make It Rain, but at low HP itself it risks dying to Draco Meteor first if Archaludon moves before it can attack.

Weighing whether Flare Blitz is still the simplest line, betting Incineroar can outspeed or that Archaludon protects again rather than attacking.

decisions.thought: Archaludon at 1% is faster than our Incineroar, so it can hit first with Electro Shot or Dracometeor and possibly KO our 82 HP Incineroar. Protect (+4) guarantees we take no damage this turn, and Archaludon dies to any later hit.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Archaludon is faster and at 1% HP, so protect reliability matters here—since Incineroar's protect already failed last turn from consecutive use, I'm weighing whether Archaludon's own protect chain is also likely to fail this turn, which could open a window for a finishing move.

Protect moves first due to priority regardless of speed, so it guarantees we block whatever Archaludon does this turn without risk. Since Incineroar at 40% HP is still valuable, Protect is the safer choice over gambling with Flare Blitz.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is faster and sits at 1% HP, so any hit finishes it. Protect is a poor choice after three consecutive uses, and Parting Shot would only bring in a 28 HP Gholdengo. Flare Blitz is the best option: Incineroar at 82 HP should survive one attack, and the move KOs if Archaludon doesn't protect again.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Archaludon is faster and at 1% HP, while Incineroar sits at 82/202. I'm checking whether Archaludon's Electro Shot, with its SpA drop factored in, can still knock out Incineroar given its Def 110, and considering the rain negating the charge turn.

Protect is a bad option now since Incineroar used it three turns in a row, dropping success chance to roughly 1/9. If Archaludon attacks with Dracometeor or Electro Shot, there's a real risk of KO'ing Incineroar given its 82 HP, so relying on protect again seems too risky.

Switching to Gholdengo via Parting Shot is tempting since it drops Archaludon's Atk/SpA further to -2, but Gholdengo at 28 HP would likely just die to Electro Shot next turn with nothing gained. Flareblitz seems like the better call if Incineroar can survive Archaludon's first move, since it would finish off the 1% HP Archaludon outright.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is at 1% and outspeeds Incineroar (94+ vs 80), so it can hit first with Electro Shot or Dracometeor and possibly KO my 82 HP Incineroar before Flare Blitz resolves. Protect has priority and avoids that hit. Incineroar's last non-Protect move was Flare Blitz on turn 13, so Protect's consecutive-use penalty has reset and should succeed. Next turn I can finish with Flare Blitz.

Protect seems like a solid option here since it has priority and lets Archaludon survive this turn to attack next, though I should factor in the consecutive-use fail chance since protect's been used recently in this match.

Flare Blitz now risks a mutual KO scenario that could leave Gholdengo exposed, so Protect is the safer choice here.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is at 1% but is faster than Incineroar, so a Flare Blitz would not land first if it attacks. Protect has +4 priority, blocks its incoming Draco Meteor or Electro Shot, and leaves it at 1% for any chip damage next turn. Parting Shot would only hand Gholdengo at 17% to a hit.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Archaludon outspeeds Incineroar even at 1% HP since it's Mega and faster (94-150 vs 80 speed), so it attacks first instead of getting hit by Flare Blitz. With Incineroar at 40.6% of 82 HP, Archaludon's Draco Meteor should be strong enough to KO it outright, though Protect is also worth considering as an option.

If Archaludon doesn't protect and attacks instead, Draco Meteor would likely KO Incineroar outright given its 130 base power. Protect is clearly the safer choice.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is at 1% and moves before Incineroar, so Flare Blitz only works if Incineroar survives its attack. Protect has likely dropped to about a one-in-three chance after two consecutive uses. Parting Shot lowers its Attack and Sp. Atk and brings in Gholdengo, which is faster and can finish the 1% Archaludon.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Archaludon is nearly dead at 1% HP but mega evolved and faster, while Incineroar sits at 40.6% and is slower. If I attack with Flare Blitz, Archaludon moves first and could hit hard enough with Draco Meteor to knock out Incineroar, so Protect looks like the safer play here given the PP I have left.

Weighing Parting Shot against Flare Blitz: gholdengo at 28 HP is fragile but could potentially outspeed and finish off archaludon at 1% HP if it switches in after the stat drop, making the trade worthwhile despite the risk.

Protect is risky since archaludon still outspeeds next turn too, and a failed Protect leaves incineroar exposed. Parting Shot guarantees the switch happens as long as incineroar survives the hit, so that's the safer line—go with parting shot.

decisions.thought: Incineroar is at 40.6% HP and slower than the 1% Archaludon, but the only legal action is switching to Gholdengo. I have to take that switch.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Switching to Gholdengo is the only legal move here, so that's what I'll go with.

decisions.thought: Archaludon is at 1% HP, so any damaging hit finishes it. Shadow Ball is neutral against Steel/Dragon, has 100% accuracy, and avoids Make It Rain's self-drop. Gholdengo might be outsped, but there's no better option.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:

decisions.hidden_reasoning:

Shadow Ball ends up as the safest option: it's neutral damage but reliable and fast enough to matter before Archaludon can fire off a potentially lethal Draco Meteor, while Make It Rain and Thunderbolt both come out weaker against this typing.
